observation.visible_scene: A near-stationary close view of a calm water surface used as a mirror: a pale blue sky reflection fills most of the frame, soft cloud-like grey swirls cross the centre, a reddish-brown autumnal branch reflection hangs from the top, and a dark conifer reflection occupies the right edge. A tiny bright speck sits near the centre and a small pale double-stripe mark is fixed at the bottom-left.
visible_changes: The reflected images (cloud swirls, top branch, right conifer) continuously and subtly deform, wobble and change extent across the segment, consistent with gentle movement of the water surface rather than any change in the objects themselves.
The wispy cloud reflection in the centre slowly reshapes and its swirl pattern drifts; the darker shadow patch in the centre-left shifts slightly in position and form.

The overall framing stays essentially constant: the bottom-left double-stripe mark and the central bright speck remain at nearly the same pixel locations, indicating the camera is fixed while only the reflection moves.
The small bright speck near the centre persists throughout with only minor jitter, staying in roughly the same spot relative to the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the surface movement (wind, a disturbance) is not visible.
Whether the bright speck is a floating object, an insect, or a specular reflection of something off-screen is unknown.
The actual scene above the water (real trees, sky) is not shown; only its reflection is visible.
Events before the first frame and after the last frame are not part of this excerpt.
uncertain_details: The drift of the reflection is hard to separate into pure deformation versus a small translation; both appear present.
Any residual camera shake is uncertain because the background reflection itself is moving.
The exact identity and motion of the central bright speck cannot be resolved at this resolution.
